title: Riyadh’s Tallest Skyscraper Struck in Houthi Attack on Saudi Wealth Fund HQ
body:
RIYADH – A missile strike on Thursday hit the Kingdom’s most prominent high‑rise, the towering headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, marking the latest escalation in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Iran‑backed Houthi rebels of Yemen. The blast, which struck the 385‑metre “Makkah Palace” tower in the capital’s financial district, caused significant damage to the building’s façade and triggered a brief evacuation of nearby offices, though no casualties have been reported. Saudi officials quickly condemned the attack as a “blatant violation of international law” and vowed to intensify defensive measures against what they describe as a growing regional threat.

The targeted structure, officially known as the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Center, is not only the tallest skyscraper in Riyadh but also a symbol of the Kingdom’s ambitious diversification agenda under Vision 2030. Designed by world‑renowned architects and completed in 2022, the tower houses the PIF’s executive suite, a hub for managing the country’s multibillion‑dollar portfolio of domestic and overseas assets. Its prominence made it a high‑value target for the Houthis, who have stepped up missile and drone operations against Saudi infrastructure since the war in Yemen entered its third year. The strike underscores the rebels’ capacity to reach deep into Saudi territory, challenging the perception that the conflict is confined to the southern border.

Analysts say the attack reflects a strategic shift by the Houthis, who have increasingly aligned their campaign with Iran’s broader regional agenda. By striking a landmark tied to Saudi economic power, the militants aim to erode confidence in the Kingdom’s ability to protect its critical assets and to pressure Riyadh into reconsidering its involvement in the Yemeni war. The timing also coincides with heightened diplomatic activity, as Saudi Arabia prepares to host a series of high‑level meetings on energy security and investment later this month. Disrupting the PIF’s headquarters could be an attempt to cast doubt on the stability of the Kingdom’s financial markets ahead of these gatherings.

The Saudi defense response was swift. Air defense systems, including the Patriot and the newer “Mistral” missile interceptors, were activated within seconds of the incoming projectile, and officials confirmed that the missile was partially neutralized before impact. However, the residual blast still managed to breach the building’s outer skin, sending shards of glass onto the streets below. Emergency services arrived promptly, and a coordinated assessment of structural integrity is underway. The Ministry of Interior announced that the area would remain under heightened security for the next 48 hours, while the PIF has issued a statement assuring investors that its operations will continue uninterrupted.

International reaction has been swift and largely condemnatory. The United Nations’ spokesperson called the strike “a dangerous escalation that threatens civilian infrastructure,” and several Western allies reiterated their support for Saudi Arabia’s right to self‑defence. Meanwhile, Tehran has denied any direct involvement, though it continues to provide political and material backing to the Houthi movement. The incident may prompt a recalibration of regional security cooperation, potentially accelerating joint missile‑defence initiatives among Gulf Cooperation Council members and their partners.

Looking ahead, the fallout from the attack could reverberate across multiple fronts. Domestically, Saudi authorities are likely to tighten security protocols around critical economic sites and may accelerate the deployment of newer air‑defence technologies. For the PIF, the incident may spur a review of contingency plans to ensure continuity of investment activities amid heightened threats. Regionally, the strike could intensify diplomatic efforts to bring the Yemeni conflict to a negotiated settlement, as the cost of unchecked escalation becomes increasingly apparent to all parties. As Riyadh rebuilds and reinforces its skyline, the episode serves as a stark reminder that even the most iconic symbols of prosperity are vulnerable in a volatile geopolitical landscape.
